subject: Micro-bundle proposal: smoothing minimums for long-context retail pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@novaretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Micro-bundle proposal: smoothing minimums for long-context retail pilot

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the time today. As promised, I sketched a micro-bundle approach that aims to balance Nova's bursty checkout workloads with long-context catalog searches. The core ask we discussed: reduce the impact of the per-request minimum when you have a mix of short session lookups and occasional long-context re-ranking passes.

High-level proposal (attached spreadsheet):
- Micro-bundle: 10k token bundle that can be consumed across sessions for a 30-day window; unused tokens roll forward for the pilot only.
- Smoothing credit: when an individual call is under the 100-token floor, apply pooling across that 1-minute window to avoid rounding up on super short calls.
- Long-context premium: for calls >8k context, apply a 1.15x multiplier to account for memory and bandwidth usage; those calls also draw from the bundle at full token weight.

Ask: can you confirm target monthly active sessions and expected % of long-context calls? I attached a baseline pricing worksheet (microbundle_pricing_table.xlsx) that shows unit economics under a few traffic mixes.

If that looks reasonable I'll loop in Procurement for the term sheet and a DocuSign.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: microbundle_pricing_table.xlsx

From: Olivia Park <olivia@novaretail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 12:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Micro-bundle proposal: smoothing minimums for long-context retail pilot

Jonas —

Appreciate the summary. Tom and I looked at the worksheet. A few clarifications:
1) What does "roll forward" mean operationally? Do unused tokens carry to the next month for the pilot or beyond?
2) For smoothing: we like pooling within a 1-minute window but want assurance this can't be gamed by client heartbeats. Any anti-abuse rules?
3) The long-context premium is fine, but can you give an example invoice line for a week where we have 90% small lookups and 10% 12k re-ranks?

Rough numbers: 120k sessions/month, avg session = 18 calls, of which 8% are re-ranks that will hit >8k.

Thanks — will need these details before I can move to Procurement.
Olivia
Head of AI Products | Nova Retail
olivia@novaretail.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@novaretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 15:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Micro-bundle proposal: smoothing minimums for long-context retail pilot

Olivia —

Great questions. Quick answers and a short example below; I also attached a draft term sheet we can use for Procurement.

1) Roll-forward: for the 90-day pilot, unused micro-bundle tokens carry forward to the following month(s) within the pilot only (no indefinite credit). After pilot close we'll either convert to a standard monthly bundle or reconcile unused tokens as a credit at renewal.

2) Anti-abuse: pooling is allowed only for requests coming from the same authenticated API key and identical downstream session id (we can require a heartbeat token). We cap pooled aggregation at 20 calls per 1-minute window and rate-limit per-key to avoid synthetic amplification. We'll include audit logs for pooled adjustments.

3) Invoice example (week sample):
- Calls: 120k sessions * 18 calls = 2,160,000 calls/month => ~540k calls/week.
- Long-context: 8% of calls = 43,200 calls/month => ~10,800/week. Assume each long-context avg = 12k tokens (prompt+response).
- Micro-bundle consumption: short calls average 40 tokens => pooled into bundles so effective billed tokens reduced by smoothing; see attached XLS for line-item math.

I'll create a quick mock invoice line for next email. Happy to hop on a 20-min call with your procurement folks.

-Jonas

Attachments: pilot-term-sheet.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Olivia Park <olivia@novaretail.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Micro-bundle proposal: smoothing minimums for long-context retail pilot

Looping in a quick mock invoice snippet so Procurement has something tangible. I'm attaching the DocuSign-ready proposal in the next email.

--- Mock invoice (week) ---
Line 1: Micro-bundle (10k tokens) — allocated 12 bundles for week => 120k tokens @ $0.004/token = $480.00
Line 2: Short-call smoothing adjustment — smoothing credit applied: 540k calls * (avg billed 40 tokens -> pool reduces effective charged tokens by 18%) => credit -$150.00
Line 3: Long-context premium — 10,800 long-context calls * 12,000 tokens * 1.15 multiplier = 149,040,000 token-equivalents @ $0.0032/token = $476,928.00
Line 4: Pilot discount (25% applied to total bundle+long-context lines) = -$119,842.00
Net (week) = $357,466.00

Notes: the long-context line dominates — we can discuss tiered step-down once traffic stabilizes. The pilot discount is negotiable but gives Nova predictable unit economics while we measure prefix reuse and KV cache benefits.

Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Tom Sanders <tom@novaretail.com>

Subject: Re: Micro-bundle proposal: smoothing minimums for long-context retail pilot

Thanks team —

Numbers make sense and the anti-abuse language is reasonable. A couple practical asks from Procurement:
- Add a clause that unused pilot tokens will be credited at the negotiated pilot rate if Nova cancels before 90 days.
- Clarify SLA on KV cache warmup for long-context calls — we need a target WPS (warm-up successfulness) so billing doesn't penalize us while caches populate.

If you can incorporate those two items in the DocuSign proposal we'll route it through our internal signoff this week.

Tom Sanders
Procurement Manager | Nova Retail
